This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Boogie-woogie right hand**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

A two-bar riff of short swung chords against the walking left hand: beat 1, the and of 1 and the and of 2 (held); then the and of 1, beat 2 and the and of 3 (held).

It belongs in *Boogie-woogie* and *Jump blues*. Here it is in the boogie-woogie style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogie-woogie right hand","opts":{"compRhythm":"boogie"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Every off-beat

Start with something simpler. A short chord on the and of every beat and never on the beat: the ska and calypso afterbeat.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-upbeats.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Every off-beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"upbeats"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Charleston

A held chord on beat 1 and a short one on the and of 2. The first comping rhythm most players learn.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-charleston.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Charleston","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Boogie-woogie right hand, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Short chords against the walking bass, a two-bar riff: 1, the and of 1, the and of 2 held; then the and of 1, 2, the and of 3 held. Keep the right hand light and swung, and play the same riff on every chord of the blues: it does not need to change, the bass does the moving.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="92" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogie-woogie right hand","opts":{"compRhythm":"boogie"}},{"label":"Charleston (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 132 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogie-woogie right hand","opts":{"compRhythm":"boogie"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|F7 F#dim7|C7|G7 F7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogie-woogie right hand","opts":{"compRhythm":"boogie"}}]'></div>

## In other styles

The same comping rhythm in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.
